## User Story

As a project maintainer running reviews across linked worktrees
I want to use one current global runtime and an activated primary project policy with explicit prior-review compatibility because cwd-based configuration and version equality can fragment policy or resume obsolete runtime code after upgrades
So that upgrades preserve review evidence without per-worktree pins or silent execution of older packages

## Scope

Design and deliver one current OS-account global AIPR runtime with activated primary-workspace project policy, classified untracked machine preferences and packaged review-collateral compatibility. Linked worktrees retain independent project dependencies and review/Git state. No exact project package-version pins or older-runtime/image fallback.

The replacement specification passed independent Claude Opus 5.5 XPR on round 3: review-a3927de204393c987234f146101239f9, accepted artifact commit 021bed7e9cc01782f0822e99fa2d3a58aadeb16e. Authority assurance is unavailable; acceptance covers design only. Implement the committed six-slice plan at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-01-102-primary-runtime-authority.md in strict sequence under parent #102. Preserve the superseded design/review as historical evidence.

#130 remains a separate detailed shared-config design; #107 owns its portable deployment/broker work. #111 collateral migration and #128 JSON formatting behavior remain constraints. This epic does not claim those open issues completed. User authorized autonomous decisions while AFK and one continuing chat; no fan-out is planned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Validated primary registration and physical Git membership reject moved/foreign/ambiguous state and caller Git environment redirection. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:1" -->
- [ ] AC2: OS-account global selection identifies the executing package and Node path; cwd/PATH/local/source/API inputs cannot impersonate it and observation digests are not equality pins. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:1" -->
- [ ] AC3: Every mutating CLI path revalidates primary/global/integration/collateral authority before effects; in-place upgrades and unchanged integration contracts remain usable. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:2" -->
- [ ] AC4: Operation classification covers every parser command, broker verb and exported writer; unclassified operations cannot mutate. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:1" -->
- [ ] AC5: Primary-exclusive authority/review/setup/host policy and user-exclusive hints/command/timing fields resolve without general deep merge; assembled automatic objects validate and hints are never identity proof. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:2" -->
- [ ] AC6: Activation requires clean committed owned blobs; missing initialized files, pre-migration/different branches, dirty/staged/unmerged owned paths and unknown activity refuse. Identical policy and unrelated merge/rebase remain valid. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:1" -->
- [ ] AC7: Doctor exposes independent registration/config/runtime/integration/format/identity/broker diagnostics; help works outside Git, closed read-only outputs remain stable, unreadable journal state remains unknown. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:2" -->
- [ ] AC8: Primary setup explicitly migrates config/shared skills/owned hooks, preserves foreign settings and current evidence, refuses linked apply and reports the primary-only command. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:2" -->
- [ ] AC9: Setup validates destination-effective formatting/lint for every tracked output before atomic writes; conflicts preserve all old bytes and host toolchain; repeated setup writes only changed bytes. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:2" -->
- [ ] AC10: Primary activation inventories active/startup/resident activity with admission fencing and committed-blob read-back; global relocations update one user record across clones. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:2" -->
- [ ] AC11: Hooks, MCP, brokers and exported writers enforce current-global selection, activated primary policy and integration currency including after asynchronous waits; no older runtime fallback. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:2" -->
- [ ] AC12: Unsupported collateral cleanup requires proven current-runtime ownership/protocol, preserves settlement evidence and cannot launch workers or execute retained images. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:2" -->
- [ ] AC13: Explicit maintenance recovery preserves literal argv and paths with spaces; preferences cannot redirect sealed active reviews and authority records ignore HOME/USERPROFILE/XDG_CONFIG_HOME/APPDATA. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:2" -->
- [ ] AC14: Each worktree retains independent untouched node_modules; consumer CI passes without AIPR installation, and multi-clone relocations use the same account registration. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:2" -->
- [ ] AC15: Compatibility schemas, setup migration, help, wrappers and bounded status match golden outputs; incompatible prior reviews stay preserved while new reviews receive independent identity and paths. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:4" -->
- [ ] AC16: Actual published tarball includes compatibility/reference/deployment verification runtime assets and excludes tests, fixtures, development scripts and source verifiers; installed fixtures cover supported Node/platforms without registry/global mutation. <!-- aitm-verified vc-list="vc:3" -->

## Deep-Dive Analysis (2026-10-01)

### Deep dive — replacement primary runtime authority for #102

The accepted replacement design is docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-102-primary-runtime-authority-design.md at 021bed7e9cc01782f0822e99fa2d3a58aadeb16e. Claude Opus 5.5 accepted XPR review-a3927de204393c987234f146101239f9 on round 3; finalization is 6abc0111f4c380f68e3b590ba5b7512d48aa6f3a. Authority assurance is unavailable. This proves design acceptance only, never implementation. Historical exact-pin design/review remain preserved as superseded evidence.

Current `src/config/load.mjs` resolves from cwd/environment and deep-merges project/user sections. `src/config/installation-identity.mjs` compares package versions and copied skill hashes. `src/protocol/compatibility.mjs` uses package-version floors; broker recovery can retain runtime images. Those mechanisms do not satisfy the accepted design. The code modules on this branch matched current trunk when examined; the earlier exact-pin specification and review remain historical evidence.

Reviewer round 3 optional notes become plan requirements: describe primary human-authored authority/review/host-policy separately from machine bindings, and validate each store's partial schema before assembling the closed `automatic` object. No modification of the accepted artifact is necessary.

The concrete implementation constraints from the accepted public-repository design are:

- One current global runtime; no exact project package-version pin and no older installed-package or retained-image fallback.
- Each worktree retains independent project dependencies and review/Git state. Never rewrite, link, or delete consumer `node_modules`.
- Primary-owned policy must be committed, clean and activated; identical owned blobs on another branch remain valid. Unrelated merge/rebase activity alone does not invalidate authority.
- Global selection uses the OS account home/profile API, never caller `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `APPDATA`. Authority-bearing Git discovery scrubs caller `GIT_*` overrides.
- Activation requires safe review inventory and read-back. Explicit setup migration preserves foreign settings and active review collateral and refuses from linked checkouts.
- An unsupported journal yields bounded diagnostics, never inferred participants, decision, state or sequence. Cleanup requires proven current ownership/protocol.
- All installed tracked outputs pass destination-effective formatting/lint before atomic writes; refuse conflicts without partial changes or host-toolchain edits.
- Consumer build/CI does not require AIPR. Source CI verifies the actual tarball on supported Windows/POSIX and Node/platform combinations.

The source inspection establishes specific gaps rather than a generic modernization. Config paths currently follow cwd and environment, and whole-section deep merge lets policy and machine preferences mingle. Installation identity currently compares package-version equality. Runtime images can retain executable code, so compatibility and recovery changes must prevent their execution rather than merely warn. Existing role, event, manifest, Git transaction and foreign ownership checks remain mandatory after the new format predicate accepts a review.

Primary policy resolves through physical Git membership and committed activated owned blobs under the validated common Git directory. Caller GIT directory/index/worktree/config overrides must be scrubbed for authority discovery. Identical committed policy on a different branch remains valid; unrelated rebase is not a policy change. Dirty, staged or unmerged owned files and unknown activation state refuse. Explicit setup does not index or commit files; activation follows clean committed owned blobs and safe review inventory with read-back. Linked setup apply points to the primary-only command.

Global selection comes from the OS account/profile API and is shared by all clones. Environment preference directories cannot redirect this record. Versions and digests are observations, not exact equality pins; in-place upgrade stays current and Node relocation edits one account record. Inventory verification must catch mixed replacement and be repeated after waits. Host identity hints remain separate from official identity proof. Validate partial primary/user automatic stores, then the assembled closed object. Machine preference changes need no project activation but cannot redirect a sealed live review.

Unsupported collateral remains preserved. Bounded status may name canonical paths and independently readable schemas/reasons, never invent participants, sequence, state or decision. Cleanup requires proved current-runtime ownership/protocol and cannot launch workers. Every CLI/MCP/hook/broker/exported writer must enforce the same selected current runner and revalidate after asynchronous waits. Consumer node_modules and CI remain independent.

The six slices have distinct stakeholder capabilities and independently reviewable tests: primary config, global selection, setup/integration activation, collateral/image fencing, cross-entrypoint enforcement and installed tarballs. Base WBS is 56 human hours; AITM converged to XL/62 with its adjustments. The old L/16 estimate is stale. Decomposition is required, and native strict sequential execution uses the existing chat without fan-out. #130 and #107 stay separate open deliverables; #111 and #128 constrain compatibility and formatting. Native broker runtime assets remain until #107 replaces them.

All seven semantic story-review questions passed for root and each task intent: real beneficiary, behavior capability, concrete source-grounded need, counterfactual prevented failure, evidence grounding, sibling distinctness and standalone readability. Each task has executable prospective verifiers and meaningful adversarial cases. Plan formatting and explicit-file Markdownlint passed; implementation verifiers have not run. The user authorized best recommendations while AFK, so decomposition and native sequence are recorded decisions, not invented human approval.
